The '''Beyer Chair''' of [[applied mathematics]] is an endowed professorial position in the [[Department of Mathematics, University of Manchester]], England. The endowment came from the will of the celebrated locomotive designer and founder of locomotive builder [[Beyer, Peacock & Company]], [[Charles Beyer|Charles Frederick Beyer]].<ref name="Hendrickson">{{cite book|author=Kenneth E. Hendrickson III|title=The Encyclopedia of the Industrial Revolution in World History|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EdwsCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA96|date=25 November 2014|publisher=[[Rowman & Littlefield]]|isbn=978-0-8108-8888-3|pages=96}}</ref><ref name="FoxGuagnini1993">{{cite book|author1=Robert Fox|author2=Anna Guagnini|title=Education, Technology and Industrial Performance in Europe, 1850-1939|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7x8AieWYGbEC&pg=PA28|date=15 July 1993|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=978-0-521-38153-6|pages=28–}}</ref><ref name="Charlton1951">{{cite book|author=Henry Buckley Charlton|title=Portrait of a University, 1851-1951: To Commemorate the Centenary of Manchester University|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FAPQAAAAIAAJ&pg=PA143|year=1951|publisher=[[Manchester University Press]]|pages=143–|id=GGKEY:KRT0GTKL14T}}</ref><ref name="Golden2017">{{cite book|author=William T. Golden|title=Science in Victorian Manchester: Enterprise and Expertise|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1TIrDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA189|date=5 July 2017|publisher=[[Taylor & Francis]]|isbn=978-1-351-49189-1|pages=189–}}</ref> He was the university's largest single donor.

The first appointment in 1881 was of Arthur Schuster who held the position until 1888.<ref name="Charlton1951"/> After Schuster's departure, the chair of Mathematics to which Horace Lamb had been appointed in 1885 became the Beyer Professorship of Mathematics and remained so until Lamb's retirement in 1920.<ref name="Golden2017"/> At this point an existing chair, of Mathematics and Natural Philosophy to which Sydney Chapman had been appointed in 1919, was renamed the Beyer Professorship of Mathematics and Natural Philosophy. After Chapman's resignation, the Beyer title was applied to the chair of Applied Mathematics. There was no incumbent between 1937 and 1945.

Most of the holders of the post were elected as [[Fellow of the Royal Society|Fellows of the Royal Society]], an honour bestowed on a small minority of UK mathematics professors. Lamb, Champman, Milne and Goldstein all received the [[Smith's Prize]] and indication of early career promise. Chapman, Goldstein and Glendinning all received the [[Adams Prize]]. 

The other endowed chairs in mathematics at the [[University of Manchester]] are the [[Richardson Professor of Applied Mathematics|Richardson Chair of Applied Mathematics]], and  the [[Fielden Professor of Pure Mathematics|Fielden Chair of Pure Mathematics]] as well as the named Sir Horace Lamb Chair.

* 1881–1888 [[Arthur Schuster]]
* 1888–1920 [[Horace Lamb]]
* 1920–1924 [[Sydney Chapman (mathematician)|Sydney Chapman]], Beyer Professor of Mathematics and Natural Philosophy <ref name="mactutorchap">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Chapman|title=Sydney Chapman}}</ref>
* 1924–1928 [[Edward Arthur Milne]]
